cells.tense: You are here with the pen, holding what's yours to hold.
cells.ask: Name one thing you carried through that's finished now, and set it down.
cells.core:
You can carry weight that's yours to carry. Not everything — the right things, the ones that are actually yours. When something heavy lands, you don't hand it off or collapse under it. You hold it, and you hold it long enough for it to change shape.

You know the difference between holding and forcing. You're not gripping. You're not waiting for someone to notice. You're just there, and it's working. The endings happening around you — you're not rushing them. You're letting them finish. That's where the strength shows. Quiet, real, and yours.
cells.sheetLine: You hold what's yours to hold, and you know when to let go.
cells.place: at the completion that allows new beginning

cells.tense: You will brace for a weight that hasn't arrived yet, and the bracing is already exhausting.
cells.ask: Let one thing end without managing it, and tell someone what that leaves you with.
cells.core:
You're already carrying what hasn't happened yet. The ending that's coming — you've rehearsed it, you've planned for it, you've taken its shape before it has one. And because you're bracing, you're not here for the part that's still open. The strength that's supposed to hold things is squeezing them instead.

Effort isn't the problem. You've got plenty. It's the exchange — letting someone else carry a piece, hearing what they see, letting give-and-take do some of the work. Bracing feels like protection. It's pressure. Let one thing finish without your hands on it, and let someone in on what that's like.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing for an ending that hasn't happened yet.

cells.tense: You stood at a door that has already closed, and some part of you is still standing there.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you carried through something that ended, and let them hear it without fixing it.
cells.core:
Something ended, and you're not through it. Not because you're weak — because you kept going without marking it. You held on through a stretch that took what you had, and when it was over, you moved straight into the next thing. The endurance is still in you. It just doesn't have anywhere to land.

Pushing harder won't do it, and feeling more won't either. Letting the ending be finished will. Not a report — a witness. When what you carried is acknowledged, the grip loosens on its own. You don't have to manufacture release. You only have to step past a closed door. Say what it took, and let that be enough.
cells.sheetLine: You carried it through and haven't gotten to say what it took.
cells.place: at the completion that allows new beginning

cells.tense: You are already holding things together in a clearing you haven't named as yours.
cells.ask: Say out loud that you're the one holding this together, plain, no qualifiers.
cells.core:
You're the one holding this. Not the situation, not the fact that nobody else stepped up. You. The persistence getting people through this ending — the quiet, unglamorous kind — it's coming from you. Someone steady in a room like this doesn't announce it. They just keep the thing upright, day after day, and call it what had to happen.

That's the gap. The work is running, and the credit goes unclaimed. Doing more won't close it. Naming what you carry will. When you say it, nothing breaks. It becomes visible — to you, and to the people leaning on you without knowing.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding this together. Nobody has heard you say so.
cells.place: at the completion that allows new beginning
